results.title: Adobe puts US online holiday spend at $275.1 billion, up 6.7%

Title: Adobe puts US online holiday spend at $275.1 billion, up 6.7%

URL Source: https://ppc.land/adobe-puts-us-online-holiday-spend-at-275-1-billion-up-6-7/

Published Time: 2026-09-29T15:39:03.000Z

Markdown Content:
_Adobe on September 28, 2026 forecast that US consumers will spend $275.1 billion on retail websites between November 1 and December 31, adding $17.3 billion to the previous season, with Cyber Monday expected to become the first day in which American online sales pass $15 billion._

## In Short

Adobe, which measures visits to US shopping websites through its analytics [software](https://ppc.land/adobe-puts-us-online-holiday-spend-at-275-1-billion-up-6-7/#), expects Americans to spend about $17 billion more online this November and December than they did a year earlier. That matters for retailers and [advertisers](https://ppc.land/adobe-puts-us-online-holiday-spend-at-275-1-billion-up-6-7/#) because more of the money is arriving through phones, pay-later plans, influencer links and AI chat tools, while classic search ads grow more slowly. Cyber Monday is expected to stay the biggest day, Black Friday is expected to grow faster, and the discounts you see are forecast to look much like last year's rather than deeper.

## A season of steady, unspectacular growth

According to Adobe, the forecast rests on Adobe Analytics data covering more than 1 trillion visits to US retail sites, 100 million[SKUs](https://ppc.land/sku/)and 18 product categories. The company describes the result as "the most comprehensive view into U.S. e-commerce", a claim it grounds in the measurement of direct online transactions rather than consumer surveys. Adobe also states that its dataset is larger than that of "any other technology company or research organization."

Discover more

Edit Media

Read Company News

Try Layout Tools

The projected growth rate of 6.7% sits almost exactly on the 6.8% that Adobe's own historical series records for 2025, when online [holiday](https://ppc.land/adobe-puts-us-online-holiday-spend-at-275-1-billion-up-6-7/#) sales reached $257.8 billion. That series, published as a chart alongside the forecast, tells a story of normalisation. Spending rose 13.1% in 2019 to $142.5 billion, jumped 32.1% in the first pandemic season of 2020 to $188.2 billion, and has since moved within a narrow band: 8.7% in 2021, 3.5% in 2022, 4.9% in 2023, 8.7% in 2024 and 6.8% in 2025. If the 2026 figure holds, US online holiday spending will have grown 93% in seven seasons.

### A revised 2024 baseline

One number in the chart does not match what Adobe said at the time.[Adobe's 2024 season results](https://ppc.land/cyber-monday-2025-preparation-requires-understanding-2024/)gave a full-season total of $240.8 billion, up 8.4%. The new chart puts 2024 at $241.4 billion, up 8.7%. The $600 million gap is small against a quarter-trillion-dollar market, and the release offers no explanation for it. Adobe's disclaimer states that the company "has no responsibility to update or revise information presented herein", yet the historical series has evidently been revised. Because every year-on-year comparison in the forecast depends on the prior-year base, the change is worth noting rather than ignoring.

## Five days, $47.5 billion

**Cyber Week**, the five days from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday, is forecast to generate $47.5 billion, up 7.4% and equal to 17.3% of the season, according to Adobe. In 2026 that window runs from Thursday, November 26 to Monday, November 30, which means the whole stretch falls inside November. In 2025, Cyber Monday landed on December 1. The season total is unaffected, since Adobe measures November 1 to December 31 in both years, but any monthly comparison will be distorted by the shift.

Cyber Monday remains the largest day, at $15.1 billion, up 6.2%. Black Friday follows at $12.9 billion, growing faster at 9.2%. Thanksgiving is forecast at $6.9 billion, up 8.5%. Subtracting those three days from the Cyber Week total leaves roughly $12.6 billion for the Saturday and Sunday combined.

Black Friday is closing the gap. Adobe's 2024 figures put Cyber Monday at $13.3 billion and Black Friday at $10.8 billion; the Friday was then worth 81% of the Monday. On the 2026 forecast, the ratio rises to 85%. Adobe gives two slightly different explanations for the acceleration. The release's summary attributes it to earlier discounts, while the body text credits Black Friday having the biggest discounts for categories such as TVs, apparel and appliances. As the discount section below shows, peak markdowns in all three of those categories are forecast to be marginally shallower than in 2025.

Discover more

Find Holiday Gifts

Get Coupons

Try Office Apps

## Where the money goes

Electronics, at $63.3 billion (up 5.9%), and apparel, at $51.3 billion (up 4.7%), remain the two largest categories, representing 23% and 18.6% of the season respectively, according to Adobe. Both are growing below the market average. The faster growth sits elsewhere: furniture at $33.4 billion (up 7.3%), grocery at $26.1 billion (up 10.3%), toys at $9.6 billion (up 9.6%) and cosmetics at $9.2 billion (up 9.5%).

Together those six categories account for $192.9 billion, or roughly 70% of the forecast. The arithmetic of growth is instructive. Grocery, at half the size of apparel, is set to add about $2.4 billion in sales against apparel's $2.3 billion, based on the growth rates Adobe supplied. Electronics adds the most in absolute terms, at roughly $3.5 billion.

### Essentials in the holiday basket

A notable part of the release concerns everyday goods rather than gifts. During Cyber Week, Adobe expects online sales of personal hygiene products to rise 150% and clothing basics 210%, with baby products up 113%, pet products up 93% and household cleaning items up 49%.

Those percentages are not year-on-year growth rates. They compare Cyber Week sales with average sales levels in September 2026, a month that had not finished when the forecast was published on September 28. The release does not say whether the baseline was measured in full or partly projected.

The pattern fits other consumer data published in recent weeks.[An Adtaxi survey of more than 1,100 US adults](https://ppc.land/40-of-americans-switch-to-lower-cost-brands-adtaxi-finds/)found 40% had switched to lower-cost brands and 93% had adopted at least one cost-saving behaviour. When Google put agentic checkout into US Search in November 2025,[its holiday guidance cited 61% of shoppers reporting more careful spending because of economic concerns](https://ppc.land/google-launches-agentic-checkout-and-ai-shopping-tools-for-holiday-season/).

## October has become a second season

Adobe expects $95.8 billion to be spent online in October 2026, up 8%, a month that sits outside the November-December window used for the headline total. The October figure alone equals about 35% of the forecast [holiday](https://ppc.land/adobe-puts-us-online-holiday-spend-at-275-1-billion-up-6-7/#) season. Nearly $10 billion of it ($9.9 billion, up 9.2%) is expected on October 6 and 7, during Amazon's October event, with discounts forecast to peak at 19% off listed price.

Discover more

Audit Your SEO

Boost SEO Traffic

Grow Your Brand

"This has changed the shape of the holiday season," Adobe wrote, arguing that retailers now have to manage promotions and inventory to capture an additional pre-season spike.

Adobe dates the October event to 2021. That does not match the event's recorded history:[Prime Big Deal Days, which Amazon scheduled for October 6-7 across 22 countries, dates back to October 2022](https://ppc.land/amazon-sets-prime-big-deal-days-for-october-6-7-across-22-countries/). The release does not clarify whether Adobe counts an earlier cross-retailer promotional period as the starting point.

The calendar around it has also moved. Amazon ran its main Prime Day from[June 23 to 26, 2026 across 26 countries](https://ppc.land/us-prime-day-ad-spend-falls-8-8-as-conversion-jumps-17-1-commerceiq-finds/), where CommerceIQ recorded US ad spend falling 8.8% while unit conversion rose 17.1%. The result is three distinct peaks in the second half of the year, all of which Amazon treats as[high velocity events](https://ppc.land/high-velocity-events/): June, October and late November.

## Discounts: deep, but no deeper

Adobe expects discounts to reach up to 30% off listed price during Cyber Week. Earlier in the season, the company forecasts markdowns of up to 14% in early November and up to 21% just before Thanksgiving, falling to 10-15% through December.

Category by category, Adobe characterises deals as "on par" with 2025. The detail supports that description, with a slight tilt toward shallower discounts:

*   **Electronics**: 30%, against 30.1% in 2025
*   **Toys**: 29%, against 28%
*   **TVs**: 23%, against 24.2%
*   **Computers**: 23%, against 22.8%
*   **Apparel**: 23%, against 23.2%

# A Record 202.9M Shoppers Turned Out Thanksgiving Weekend

Black Friday is still the most popular shopping day over the five-day holiday weekend, as per the National Retail Federation’s survey.

[![Image 35](https://uploads.nationaljeweler.com/uploads/7aa17c3727ee24de764af5c00ad5b62b.jpg)](https://nationaljeweler.com/search_by_authors?query=Lenore+Fedow)[Lenore Fedow](https://nationaljeweler.com/search_by_authors?query=Lenore+Fedow)[lenore.fedow@nationaljeweler.com](mailto:lenore.fedow@nationaljeweler.com)

![Image 36: Shoppers in a mall](https://uploads.nationaljeweler.com/uploads/fff74b689fce1f0e22448b75b7a56181.jpg)

In its annual survey, the National Retail Federation shared insights into the five-day holiday weekend shopping period.

Washington, D.C.—A record-breaking 202.9 million consumers shopped over the five-day holiday weekend from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, according to the National Retail Federation (NRF).  
  
The NRF, alongside Prosper Insights & Analytics, released the annual survey Tuesday, tallying up who hit the stores, who shopped online, what they bought, and more.  
  
This year’s turnout exceeded the 197 million shoppers last year and surpassed the previous record of 200.4 million set in 2023.  
  
It also beat the NRF’s initial expectations of 186.9 million shoppers over the holiday weekend.  
  
“This year’s record turnout reflects a highly engaged consumer who is focused on value, responds to compelling promotions, and seizes upon the opportunity to make the winter holidays special and meaningful,” said NRF President and CEO Matthew Shay.  
  
On a media call Tuesday, Shay was joined by Phil Rist, executive vice president of strategy at Prosper Insights & Analytics, to discuss the results.  
  
Online shopping was the most popular option, with 134.9 million shoppers, up 9 percent year-over-year, while 129.5 million consumers shopped in stores, up 3 percent year-over-year.

results.title: Adobe projection: 2026 online holiday sales to reach $275.1 billion
results.markdown:
Title: Adobe projection: 2026 online holiday sales to reach $275.1 billion

URL Source: https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/09/29/adobe-projection-2026-online-holiday-sales-275-billion/amp/

Published Time: 2026-09-29T14:51:57+00:00

Markdown Content:
![Image 1: Adobe's forecast for the 2026 holiday shopping season projects online sales in the last two months of the year will reach $275.1 billion. | Image credit: kerkezz - Adobe Stock](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AdobeStock_466781601-1024x453.jpeg)
Adobe's forecast for the 2026 holiday shopping season projects online sales in the last two months of the year will reach $275.1 billion. | Image credit: kerkezz - Adobe Stock

Adobe has released its forecast for the 2026 holiday shopping season, projecting that online sales in the last two months of the year will reach $275.1 billion.

It said it based its forecast on more than 1 trillion visits to U.S. retail sites, 100 million SKUs and 18 product categories. The company refers to the holiday shopping season as Nov. 1 through Dec. 31.

The projection indicates that online holiday-season sales in 2026 would increase 6.7% year over year. Within that period, Adobe anticipates sales during the [Cyber 5](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/cyber-5-highlights/) to reach $47.5 billion. That would represent 7.4% year-over-year growth, in addition to 17.3% of 2026’s total online holiday sales.

The Cyber 5 refers to the five-day period that runs from [Thanksgiving](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/thanksgiving-ecommerce-sales/) through [Cyber Monday](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/cyber-monday-online-sales/).

Adobe anticipates six categories to lead 2026 holiday-season online sales:

1.   Electronics ($63.3 billion, which would mark a 5.9% year-over-year increase)
2.   Apparel ($51.3 billion, up 4.7%)
3.   Furniture ($33.4 billion, up 7.3%)
4.   Grocery ($26.1 billion, up 10.3%)
5.   Toys ($9.6 billion, up 9.6%)
6.   Cosmetics ($9.2 billion, up 9.5%)

## Adobe’s anticipated online sales trends during the 2026 holiday season

The Adobe projection indicates Cyber Monday surpassing $15 billion in online sales — setting a new bar for the most in a single day. In total, consumers spent $14.25 billion in ecommerce sales on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe. Its projection has Cyber Monday generating $15.1 billion online in the U.S., which would mark 6.2% year-over-year growth.

That would continue a trend in which each year since 2022, Cyber Monday has set records for the most ecommerce sales in a single day.

Adobe also projects Black Friday will be the second-largest day during the holiday season in terms of sales. It anticipates Black Friday sales in 2026 reaching $12.9 billion, increasing 9.2% year over year.

Furthermore, Adobe anticipates Thanksgiving Day ecommerce sales to reach $6.9 billion in 2026. That would mark 8.5% growth on a day that Adobe projects 63% of all online sales to come from mobile devices. 61.6% of all Thanksgiving Day ecommerce sales came from mobile devices in 2025, per Adobe.

In total throughout the 2026 holiday shopping season, Adobe projects 57.4% of online sales to come from mobile devices. That would mark an increase from 56.4% the year before.

Buy now, pay later (BNPL) could generate $21.3 billion in holiday-season ecommerce sales, Adobe said, up 6.6%. And on Cyber Monday alone, BNPL usage could account for $1.09 billion. Cyber Monday 2025 marked the first time BNPL-related ecommerce sales surpassed $1 billion in a single day. Adobe also projects BNPL spending for online orders to reach $807 million on Black Friday 2026.

## Impact of AI platforms on 2026 holiday season’s sales

Adobe first began measuring how consumers use artificial intelligence (AI)-based chat and browser services for online shopping during the [2024 holiday season](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2025/01/07/online-holiday-sales-us-global-2024/).

Compared to October 2024, when generative AI platforms such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT became more widespread, AI-referral traffic has [increased 1,219% in July 2026](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/08/19/adobe-ai-referral-traffic-data-july-2026/), Adobe found. That was also 62% year-over-year growth in July.

In the 2026 holiday shopping season, Adobe projects AI traffic to U.S. retail sites to increase 130% year over year. It expects the largest increases on:

*   Thanksgiving, at 159% year-over-year growth
*   Black Friday, 95% increase
*   Cyber Monday, 88% increase

Additionally, Adobe shared insights from a survey it conducted of 5,000 online shoppers. It found that 77% of respondents who have used AI for online shopping reported feeling more confident in their purchase. 69% of respondents said they were less likely to return an item they bought.

## Pre-holiday-season sales boost

And leading up to the holiday season, Adobe anticipates U.S. consumers will spend $95.8 billion online during October 2026. That would be 8% more than the same month in 2025. Adobe attributes that growth, in part, to [Amazon’s Prime Day event in October](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/article/everything-about-amazon-prime-day/), which leads other online retailers to offer their own discounts to compete.

Specifically, Adobe anticipates U.S. consumers spending $10 billion online during the 48-hour Amazon Prime Day event period on Oct. 6 and 7.

results.title: NRF Expects Holiday Sales Growth
results.markdown:
Title: NRF Expects Holiday Sales Growth

URL Source: https://hardwareretailing.com/holiday-sales-growth-expected-nrf-says/

Published Time: 2024-11-18T15:56:51+00:00

Markdown Content:
![Image 1: Holiday Sales Growth](https://hardwareretailing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/HOlidayGiftShopping_Featured.jpg)

[Jacob Musselman](https://hardwareretailing.com/author/jmusselman/)November 18, 2024[Industry News](https://hardwareretailing.com/category/latest-news/)

A record [183.4 million people](https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/record-number-shoppers-expected-over-thanksgiving-holiday-weekend) are planning to shop in-store and online from Thanksgiving Day through Cyber Monday this year, according to the[National Retail Federation (NRF) Holiday survey](https://nrf.com/research-insights/holiday-data-and-trends/winter-holidays). The figure is up from the previous record of 182 million in 2023 and 18.1 million more people than five years ago in 2019.![Image 2](http://hardwareretailing.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/pr1_2024_thanksgiving_weekend_expected_shopping-300x145.jpg)

“Even though holiday shopping continues to pull forward, some of the busiest shopping days of the year are during the five-day Thanksgiving weekend,” says Katherine Cullen, NRF vice president of industry and consumer insights. “Consumers are prioritizing gift-giving for the most important people in their lives, and retailers are prepared to help customers find everything on their shopping lists at great prices throughout the season.”

57% of shoppers plan to shop during Thanksgiving weekend because of deals and discounts, 28% plan to shop because of tradition and 24% reported they like to start holiday shopping early.

While consumers will spread their shopping across channels throughout the five-day holiday weekend, Black Friday remains the most popular day to shop, with 72%, or 131.7 million people planning to go to stores or shop online. About two-thirds of Black Friday shoppers expect to specifically shop in stores that day. Cyber Monday is the second most popular day, attracting 39%, or 72.3 million of those planning to shop.![Image 3](http://hardwareretailing.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/pr2_2024_thanksgiving_weekend_expected_shopping-300x175.jpg)

The trend of early holiday shopping continues with 58% of consumers having already started their holiday shopping as of early November.

“Younger shoppers are most likely to take advantage of Thanksgiving weekend deals this year, with 89% of young adults between 18-24 planning to shop over the weekend,” says Phil Rist, Prosper Insights & Analytics executive vice president of strategy. “The social aspect of holiday shopping is also enticing to this age group, and they are most likely to shop because it’s a group activity that can be enjoyed with friends and family.”

Half of the interviewed consumers not currently planning to shop during the holiday weekend could be convinced to do so if items they want are on sale or if friends or family invite them.

Data released by the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/census-data-october-shows-healthy-retail-sales-and-early-step-forward) shows retail sales grew the past two months. The growth represents households’ capacity to spend and the strength in the economy, says [Jack Kleinhenz](https://hardwareretailing.com/nrf-predicts-holiday-sales-growth/), NRF chief economist.

“October’s pickup in retail sales shows a healthy pace of spending as many consumers got an early start on holiday shopping,” Kleinhenz says. “October sales were a good early step forward into the holiday shopping season, which is now fully underway. Falling energy prices have likely provided extra dollars for household spending on retail merchandise.”

# Edit your Business Profile

You can edit your verified Business Profile on Google to keep your business info accurate and up to date. You can update details like your address, hours, contact info, and photos to help customers find and learn more about your business.

[Manage your business](https://business.google.com/?skipLandingPage=true&gmbsrc=ww-ww-et-gs-z-gmb-v-z-h~bhc-core-u|mybb)

**Important****:**

*   To show your business on Search, Maps, and other Google services, you must [add or claim your business](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2911778) then [verify your Business Profile](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242).
*   Some businesses might need to verify their Business Profile first before they can make any changes with their info.

## Edit a Business Profile

You can edit your Business Profile directly on Search or Maps. Certain features to manage your profile may differ between Search and Maps and your device's operating system.

[Video 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zyfqSKierWU)

**Important:** To edit your business info, you need to sign in to the Google Account that's linked to your Business Profile.

### [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)Edit your Business Profile on Google Search

1.   [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2.   Select **Edit profile**.
3.   After you make your changes, select **Save**.

### Edit your Business Profile with the Google Maps app

1.   On your mobile device, open the Google Maps app ![Image 4: Maps](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/yBT9NcPCOum61BXUrmlfBecOpNufMGBDbh3rFQfIQu1Rs23tjRnhNdEou6yHAurnyw=h36).
2.   At the bottom right, tap **Business**.
3.   Tap **Edit profile**.
4.   After you make your changes, tap **Save**.

### [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)Suggest an edit to someone else's Business Profile

*   If you find something wrong with a Business Profile that you don’t own or manage, you can [suggest an edit](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/7084895).
*   If someone else's business is missing from Google Maps, you can [add a missing place](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6320846).

## Review information collected by Google

**Important:**This feature is currently available for select regions, languages, and business categories and may not be available for all users.

To confirm your business details and keep your Business Profile updated and discoverable for customers looking for businesses like yours, Google may occasionally reach out using automated messages via call, text, or WhatsApp to the verified phone number on your profile.

Any information you provide in response to these messages may be used to update your profile. [Learn more about automated calls and texts from Google to confirm business info](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7690269).

To review and manage this collected information:

1.   [Go to your Business Profile](https://business.google.com/).
2.   Select **Edit profile**![Image 5: and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/LXIVMHxIoJ-ODytEi75yC-dtUFJFsRd6p8dopSSRr_ZUOPKvyuUgsU-7zVNA6ui8LmRz=h36)**Collected info**.
3.   Review the information to confirm its accuracy. 
    *   You can also find the source of this info and the date it was collected.
    *   This information displays in the language it was originally provided in.

4.   If you want to remove a piece of information, select **Delete**![Image 6: and then](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/LXIVMHxIoJ-ODytEi75yC-dtUFJFsRd6p8dopSSRr_ZUOPKvyuUgsU-7zVNA6ui8LmRz=h36)**Delete**. 
    *   **Tip:**Deleting collected information removes it from Google's records but does not change other details already on your Business Profile.

## [](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)Types of edits

Here are some details and tips for the kind of info you can add or edit on your Business Profile.

We [review your changes](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038311) before we update them live on your profile. [Learn more about our guidelines for representing your business](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177).

[Check your edit status](https://support.google.com/business/workflow/15989794)

[Business name](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

Enter your business name exactly as it appears on your real world business signage, stationery, and other branding. If you change your business name after it’s verified, you might need to verify your business again. [Learn more about Business Profile quality guidelines](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177).

[Category](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

Select the category that best matches what your business does. All locations of a business must share a “Primary category.” Choose a specific category that represents your main business. If you select several categories, the category in the first field will be your primary category. [Learn more about how to manage your business category](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7249669).

You can select up to 9 more categories. If you have trouble choosing a category for your business, choose one that’s general.

**Tips:**

*   Do not use categories solely as keywords or to describe features of your business.
*   Do not use categories that match other nearby or related businesses.  
**Example:**
    *   A business that’s located inside your business’s physical location
    *   Another business that your business is located inside.

[Address and pin location](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

Enter the full and accurate address of your business location. [Learn more about address entry guidelines](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2853879).

*   **If you don't****meet****customers at your business address,**you can choose to not show your address. [Learn how to remove your address](https://support.google.com/business/answer/2853879#removegmb).
*   **If you****move****your****business to a new address****after****it’s****verified,** you must [verify your business again](https://support.google.com/business/topic/4854193).

[Service area](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

If your business serves customers within a specific local area, enter your service area. When you list your service area, this helps people know if you can visit or deliver to their location.

You can set your service area based on the cities, zip codes, or other places you serve. [Learn about how to set your service area](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481).

**Tip:** When you set your service area, be as specific and accurate as possible.

[Hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

*   To update your customers on when you’re open, [set your business’s main hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/10417060#set_hour) or [mark it closed](https://support.google.com/business/answer/15300196). 
*   To change your hours for holidays or other temporary periods, [set special hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/6303076#holiday_hours).
*   If you have different hours for different features you offer, [set more hours](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9876800#more_hour).

[Phone number](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3039617)

In addition to your primary business phone number, you can enter up to 2 more phone numbers. They can be mobile numbers or landline, but not fax.

**Tip:** You can choose to hide your phone number on your Business Profile.
